faqs.q: Why does my breaker keep tripping?
faqs.a: Circuit breakers trip when the circuit is overloaded or when there is a short from the hot wire to neutral or ground. Shorts trip the breaker immediately, while it may take time for an overloaded circuit to trip. Remove one device at a time to reduce the load, and if the circuit still trips often, it may indicate more severe problems.

faqs.q: What are the risks of overloading a circuit?
faqs.a: An overloaded circuit can allow the wires inside your wall to heat up and start a fire. Most household circuits are rated at 15 amps, and if you exceed that significantly, the circuit breaker should trip. Avoid using extension cords or outlet strips, and if you must, make sure they are rated appropriately for the devices connected to them.

faqs.q: Can I do my own electrical work?
faqs.a: It is not only dangerous, it can even be illegal if you do not have a permit. Shoddy electrical repairs can lead to fires, electrocution and device failure, so it is not worth the risk.

faqs.q: When should you have an electrical safety check?
faqs.a: A safety check ensures that your property is safe after years of potential neglect. It should be performed every five years. You should also request one if you are moving into a home that is over 25 years old. The process tests the safety of your circuits and identifies overloading.

faqs.q: Which problems require an emergency electrician?
faqs.a: Any time your safety or comfort has been seriously compromised. A power outage inside the home while your neighbors have power, an overheating or smoking outlet, sparks from an outlet or light switch, a broken breaker, a buzzing or overheated panel, damaged or exposed wiring, or a repair needed to keep medical equipment working.
